business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchandising of Fashion Jewelry and Fine Timepieces

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, as amended, Articles 1, 12, 128, 154, 156, 192, 208, 212, 228 and 412, together with the Foreign Investment Act, Articles 6, 7 and 8
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation with Affidavit of Compliance
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan Company Act does not impose a minimum authorized paid-in capital for a limited liability company. The amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid up and deposited in a bank account; a temporary capital verification deposit is required before registration. The funds may be released after the company receives its company registration certificate and unified business tax number. There is no statutory blocked-escrow requirement except a foreign investment approval letter may condition the capital remittance on evidence of the bank deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LTD. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the authorized and issued share capital of the Company, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, is fully subscribed by the sole foreign shareholder in the amount of [capital amount] divided into [number] shares with [par value] per share, and that the paid-up portion shall be deposited by the responsible officers into a temporary capital verification bank account at [Bank Name] in Taiwan, to be released only upon completion of company registration and foreign investment approval. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Board authorizes the Chairman, President, and Company Secretary, or any two acting together, to open and operate the Company's commercial banking, foreign currency, and payroll accounts at [Bank Name], to execute account agreements, to designate approved signatories, and to file any central bank foreign exchange reporting as required. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Address], Taiwan, and management is directed to execute the lease agreement, obtain landlord consent, and post the statutory signboard at such address as the Company's legal seat for receipt of process. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the following individuals are hereby appointed as statutory officers of the Company: [Name] as Chairman and Director; [Name] as Director; [Name] as Supervisor; [Name] as President and General Manager; and [Name] as Company Secretary. Each officer shall serve until the next shareholders' meeting and shall exercise the duties prescribed by the Taiwan Company Act, including issuance of shares, maintenance of the shareholder register, preparation and audit of financial statements, calling of shareholders' meetings, and preservation of corporate records. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Chairman, the President, and the Company Secretary are jointly and severally delegated to prepare and submit the company registration application, to obtain the unified business tax number, to engage the registered accounting firm, and to take all lawful actions necessary to carry out this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Review and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, via its online Foreign Investment Application System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investment application through the online portal of the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, before filing the company registration. The application must be accompanied by the foreign investor's audited financial statements or a recent bank reference letter, notarized corporate authorization, beneficial ownership declaration, a business plan describing the online retail of fashion jewelry and timepieces, and the approved company name reservation. Execute all signing pages before a Taiwan notary or legalize the foreign signatures by apostille. Within the administrative correction period, provide the Commission with any missing information in the requested form. The Commission will issue a formal investment approval letter, which is the basis for capital remittance and subsequent registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation or passport of the foreign shareholder
Power of attorney and identity documents
Beneficial ownership organizational chart and declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit a targeted correction letter and supporting exhibits within 15 days. If the application is suspended, request a formal administrative consultation or hearing. A denial may be appealed by administrative petition within 30 days after receipt of the written decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Organizational Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Notary Public Office and the licensed bank selected for the capital verification deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the sole corporate shareholder to approve the Articles of Incorporation, subscribed capital, initial directors and supervisor, and the first board resolution. Prepare and execute all organizational documents, including the company name, business scope, registered office address, capital amount, and statutory officers. Have the corporate seal engraved and notarized if required by the bank or registry. Certify the signatures before a Taiwan notary. Deposit the paid-in capital into a temporary capital verification bank account at a licensed bank and obtain a deposit certificate or provisional bank statement. The first board resolution must instruct management to open operating bank accounts only after the company registration is complete.
required_dossiers: Capital verification bank deposit certificate or provisional bank statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects or returns the documents, amend the inconsistent provisions and re-execute the corrected pages before the same notary. Any corrected signature page must be attached as an exhibit to the subsequent company registration filing. Additional notarization may be required for each revised capital or officer provision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Company Registration and Tax Number Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the National Taxation Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company registration application online at the Ministry of Economic Affairs company registration portal, attaching the investment approval letter, notarized organizational documents, capital verification certificate, lease agreement, and landlord consent for the registered office. Submit the affidavit of compliance confirming all filings are lawful and accurate. After the Department of Commercial Affairs approves the registration, obtain the company registration certificate. Then register with the local National Taxation Bureau to receive the unified business tax number and VAT registration. The company must not refund paid-in capital to the shareholder before the registration and tax number are completed.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of directors, supervisor, and responsible person
Registered office lease agreement and landlord consent certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction notice, cure the deficiency within 30 days by amending and resubmitting the specified attachments. If the registration is rejected for a material defect, file a fresh application and pay the reduced re-filing fee under the Company Registration Fee Schedule. Tax number mismatches can be corrected by submitting a written correction request to the local National Taxation Bureau.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Banking, Labor, and Tax Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Taiwanese commercial bank, National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Labor, Labor Insurance Bureau, and National Health Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the company registration certificate is issued, open the company's active operating bank account by presenting the registration certificate, unified business tax number certificate, corporate seal, and board resolution appointing account signatories. Complete foreign exchange reporting with the Central Bank of Taiwan through the receiving bank for the injected capital. Register the company as an employer with the labor insurance and national health insurance authorities. File the responsible person registration with the National Taxation Bureau for payroll withholding and VAT filing obligations. Maintain the corporate books, bank statements, and shareholder register in accordance with Taiwan tax law and accounting standards.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal and responsible person identification
Employer registration forms for labor and health insurance
Foreign exchange remittance approval and Central Bank reporting forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For bank compliance or de-risking query, provide updated beneficial ownership certification, registered office proof, and a refreshed board resolution renewing the signatory list. For insurance or tax registration mismatches, submit a written amendment to the relevant bureau and align the effective dates with the company registration certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial manufacturing, chemical processing, physical product assembly, or regulated warehousing license is required for a Taiwan company engaged in ISIC 4791 online retail of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no factory registration, manufacturing license, or special industrial operation permit is required under the Statute for Industrial Innovation or the Taiwan Company Act for an online merchandising company.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment report and environmental registration because the activity is a non-industrial trading service with no manufacturing or regulated physical processing operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero process wastewater discharge, zero regulated VOC exhaust emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation. If the company later adds consolidated distribution warehousing of non-hazardous retail goods, it must arrange municipal waste collection but remains below the statutory industrial discharge thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire safety permit is required because no factory, hazardous-chemical warehouse, or assembly line is operated. The registered office must nevertheless maintain standard fire alarms, fire extinguishers, and building safety compliance, and the local fire department structural inspection certificate should be available for commercial building occupancy. General workplace safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act apply to employees working in the office and retail environment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online administration through the China Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal of the relevant provincial tax service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation, the WFOE must complete tax registration with the local STA office within 30 days after the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) issues the business license. The SAMR-issued Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) serves as the legal tax identification number (TIN). Submission includes foreign investment filing, articles of association, registered address proof, legal representative identification, and bank account details. The WFOE must then register for VAT with the STA office and, if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed RMB 5,000,000, apply for General VAT taxpayer status. For export activities, the WFOE must complete export tax refund registration and customs registration in the China International Trade Single Window to obtain an exporter code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election to a resident WFOE; the entity is taxed separately as a resident enterprise. The WFOE may only elect simplified small-scale VAT treatment below the statutory threshold or special tax treatment in qualifying corporate reorganizations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All WFOEs must complete tax registration regardless of turnover; mandatory General VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax System Phase IV requiring fully digitalized electronic invoices (FDEI). VAT invoices must be issued through STA-approved systems, transmitted in real time to the tax authority via system-to-system API, and secured by cryptographic anti-fraud digital stamps and the required tax control key.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods are eligible for the 0% VAT rate under the PRC VAT legal framework. The WFOE must be a General VAT taxpayer, the goods must physically leave the Chinese customs territory under a valid customs export declaration, a genuine offshore sale to the buyer must be documented, and export proceeds must be received and verified in accordance with SAFE rules. Cross-border e-commerce exports must be made through an eligible platform and appear in customs statistical records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Declaration (Declaration Form for Exported Goods)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Export Proceeds Verification Certificate / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective STA review. If documentation is false, incomplete, or proceeds are not repatriated within the deadline, the claimed VAT refund will be clawed back, the supply will be reclassified as taxable at the standard VAT rate, a daily late-payment surcharge will apply, and administrative penalties of 50% to five times the unpaid tax may be imposed. Fraudulent export refund applications may also trigger criminal liability, customs disqualification, and loss of future zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is current-account convertible: for genuine goods and service transactions, a WFOE may convert trade-related FX receipts and make payments through SAFE-authorized banks by submitting the customs declaration, invoice, contract and transaction documents. Capital account convertibility remains heavily controlled: inbound FDI equity injection must be registered under the SAFE FDI registration system, deposited into a dedicated FDI foreign exchange capital account, converted to RMB only through bank-supervised settlement, and each capital RMB payment must be backed by an actual operating expenditure (procurement, salary, rent, tax, royalties). Dividends to the Taiwan parent are treated as profit remittance under the current account and require audited financial statements, tax clearance, a board distribution resolution and bank verification; the bank will not process dividend remittance if the WFOE has unreconciled cross-strait tax or debt obligations. Export proceeds must be repatriated to China and retained in a foreign currency account or sold to a designated bank; there is no mandatory conversion ratio under the current trade monitoring framework, but overdue export receipts beyond 90 days must be explained and reported to SAFE. Overall, liquidity planning must assume PBOC/SAFE documentation lead times and real-demand verification on every FX conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be repatriated into the WFOE's domestic foreign-exchange current account within the trade payment term evidenced by the customs declaration and contract; any receipts falling outside the 90-day monitoring window must be reported through the bank's trade foreign exchange monitoring system as advance/trailing receipts. The mandatory surrender ratio is zero: a WFOE may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency or sell them to a designated FX bank at the benchmark spot rate, but every RMB conversion must be covered by the original customs declaration, commercial invoice, packing list, logistics documents and the SAFE trade digital record.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account); RMB Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account); RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
RMB Basic Operational Currency Account; Cross-Border RMB Trade Settlement Account
RMB Basic Operational Currency Account; Multi-Currency Operating and Customs Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low / not viable for primary banking and clearing. In mainland China, foreign fintech EMI brands (Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not licensed by PBOC as banks and are legally barred from opening local RMB or foreign exchange accounts, holding deposits, or performing SAFE-controlled settlement for a WFOE. They may be used only as auxiliary acquiring/collection processors for cross-border e-commerce (Stripe/PayPal can connect to domestic payment institutions and route buyer funds into a licensed domestic bank). All regulated FX, customs tax, payroll and capital account payments must ultimately clear through a PBOC-supervised commercial bank or a licensed domestic payment institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a first-time corporate account opening by a Taiwan-invested WFOE, the statutory legal representative must appear physically at the bank branch with original identity documents, passport/Taiwan travel permit and the company chop. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted under PBOC account-opening rules; an authorized signatory may attend with a notarized and cross-strait-authenticated power of attorney, but the bank still requires a live video confirmation with the legal representative and an in-person interview for the senior accountable officer. Some banks may waive physical presence for a fully notarized POA only after the legal representative completes a recorded bank video call, but this remains an exception, not a standard onboarding right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity: the Taiwan parent entity is controlled through multiple private investment holding layers or nominee shareholders, creating a red flag for unidentified principal risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group ownership chart; BVI/Singapore/Hong Kong/Taiwan certificates of incorporation and register of directors/shareholders; notarized and authenticated UBO declaration identifying every natural person with more than 10% economic interest; passport copies and proof of residential address for each UBO; Taiwan MOEA company registration extracts; professional intermediary confirmation from the formation agent; audited financial statements for each holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Luxury watches and fashion jewelry e-commerce profile triggers higher-risk product/merchant screening, trade-based money laundering potential, counterfeit brand infringement exposure, and inconsistent declared/actual goods value.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete supplier contracts and purchase orders; item-level product catalog with batch/lot codes; certificates of authenticity, hallmark/carat reports for precious metals; customs export declarations and import records; logistics airway bills and freight forwarding receipts; e-commerce platform payout reports from Stripe/PayPal; chargeback and refund historical schedules; independently audited revenue reconciliation of platform settlements to bank deposits; trademark/IP ownership or authorization licenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic substance deficiency: the WFOE has no meaningful office, payroll, or physical operations but projects high-velocity online jewelry/watch sales, raising shell-company and conversion-to-cash concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease agreement with real-site photos; payroll records and social insurance payment vouchers; utility bills and property management receipts; corporate income tax and VAT filings with tax payment certificates; third-party logistics and fulfillment center contracts; annual financial statements audited by a China-licensed CPA; bank statements showing recurring operating expenditure (rent, salaries, platform fees, insurance).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait fund origin/investment legitimacy and sanctions/PEP exposure: investor funding originates from Taiwan without clear regulatory approvals, and counterparties may include high-risk jurisdictions or politically exposed persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Taiwan Investment Commission (MOEA) mainland investment approval or legally authenticated cross-strait investment filing; SAFE FDI registration record; source-of-funds evidence for the equity injection (bank credit advice, tax-paid dividend distribution records, encumbrance-free capital); sanctions/PEP screening reports covering all shareholders and counterparties; SWIFT BIC/LEI confirmation of correspondent banks; OFAC/EU/UN sanctions database search results; negative news and global PEP database report; written corporate undertaking that no proceeds originate from illegal or sanctioned activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan investor should remit in USD or another freely convertible currency by SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's dedicated FDI foreign exchange capital account at a PBOC-licensed bank. Before remittance, the WFOE must complete SAFE FDI registration and open the capital account using its unified social credit code and foreign investment information report. The MT103 narrative must carry the SAFE foreign exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment equity contribution (non-resident direct investment paid-in capital) and reference the WFOE entity name and FDI registration record reference number. Upon credit, a Chinese certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report; the funds may then be settled into RMB under the bank's payment-purpose settlement process, with each RMB payment linked to genuine operating transactions (purchase of goods, payroll, rent, tax, third-party logistics). The Taiwan-side remitter must also provide the Taiwan Investment Commission approval or legally authenticated investment filing, a board resolution for capital increase, and source-of-funds bank records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier/trade payments, use direct SWIFT MT103 wires from the WFOE's FX current account for high-value one-off disbursements; for repetitive procurement of jewelry components, use cross-border RMB settlement through the CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) or correspondent bank SWIFT if the supplier accepts RMB. For larger import purchase orders, issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit through the WFOE's account bank, with a confirming bank for high-risk jurisdictions; for lower-value, document-based orders, use documentary collections (D/P or D/A) through the advising bank. Every outbound payment must be matched with the customs declaration, invoice, purchase contract, and SAFE trade-in-services/goods transaction code; the bank will block payments lacking business background or containing sanctioned parties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD FX forwards with a licensed domestic

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report on Directors, Supervisors, Managers and Major Shareholders / Beneficial Owners (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Company and Commercial Registration Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for the preceding calendar year; any change in directors, managers, controlling shareholders, or beneficial owners must be reported within 15 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or false filing is subject to a fine of TWD 50,000 to TWD 500,000 (approx. USD 1,560 to USD 15,625) per violation, plus a MOEA corrective order; recurring violations are fined repeatedly; persistent noncompliance combined with six months of inactive operations may trigger an administrative dissolution order, equivalent to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders Approval of Business Report, Financial Statements, and Earnings Distribution Proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; executed resolution retained in the corporate Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each fiscal year-end, i.e. by 30 June for a 31 December year-end; a special fiscal year must have prior MOEA approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to lay final accounts before shareholders or to hold the annual meeting within the six-month window subjects the responsible person to MOEA fines of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000 (approx. USD 313 to USD 1,563) per violation; prolonged dormancy may result in MOEA administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Shareholder-Approved Annual Financial Statements with the Company Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after shareholder approval and no later than 15 July for a 31 December fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers a MOEA order to rectify within a prescribed period; failure to rectify attracts repeated fines of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000 (approx. USD 313 to USD 1,563) per offense; if the entity is dormant, MOEA may revoke or dissolve the company registration after 30 days demand notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and Supporting Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (local jurisdiction office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities, filing is due annully between 1 May and 31 May of the following year; approved special fiscal year filings are due within one month after the approved fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes an additional tax of 3% of the underpaid tax for every two weeks overdue, capped at 10%, plus interest at the applicable post office one-year deposit rate; continued non-filing authorizes the tax authority to assess income by estimation, subject the company to tax liens, and support an administrative dissolution referral to MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Investment Operation Report (for approved foreign-invested company status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May following the reporting fiscal year; within 30 days of any MOEA demand when a non-calendar fiscal year has been approved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in suspension or revocation of the foreign-investment approval after a 30-day cure notice, restrictions on outward remittance and capital repatriation, and fines of up to TWD 300,000 (approx. USD 9,375); habitual non-filing may be used as evidence for MOEA administrative strike-off.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate under Article 4 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential rates: 15% for High/New Technology Enterprises (HNTE) under Article 28; effective reduced rate of 5% or 10% for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million; 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; additional regional or free-trade-zone incentives may apply for encouraged industries (e.g., software, integrated circuits); e-commerce income may qualify for simplified taxable income assessment in certain comprehensive-bonded zones.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form A, A100000) filed through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal, along with supporting schedules such as A105000 (Tax Adjustment Items) and A107000 (Tax Incentives).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional filings with annual final settlement; quarterly returns due within 15 days after each quarter-end; annual return due within 5 months after the tax year-end (May 31 of the following calendar year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly: within 15 days after the end of March, June, September, and December; Annual: by May 31 of the following year; the tax year is the Gregorian calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Revenue - total revenue from online sales of jewelry, watches, and fashion accessories via e-commerce platforms (Stripe, PayPal).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross sales including platform refunds and chargebacks; for cross-border sales, revenue should be converted to RMB using the exchange rate published by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) at the time of recognition. Warning: under-reporting e-commerce revenue due to undisclosed PayPal or Stripe settlement accounts is a common red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Costs - directly attributable cost of goods sold, including procurement from suppliers, raw materials, and manufacturing overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If intercompany purchases from Taiwanese affiliate exceed RMB 20 million, maintain comparable price documentation; a low cost-to-revenue ratio may trigger transfer pricing scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and Surcharges - consumption tax, city maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, and other levies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For e-commerce entities, VAT is declared separately; ensure that VAT payable is not mistakenly included in this line, as only non-VAT taxes belong here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling Expenses - advertising, logistics, platform commissions, payment gateway fees, shipping and packaging.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment gateway charges (Stripe/PayPal) are deductible only if supported by valid receipts from approved foreign-exchange settlement; payments to overseas marketing affiliates may require withholding tax if the services are performed in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative Expenses - salaries, rents, professional fees, and general overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Salaries payable to Taiwanese expatriate directors are deductible only if the individual is registered with Chinese social insurance and individual income tax is withheld; rent payments to a related offshore entity will be disallowed if lacking economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial Expenses - interest expense, bank charges, and foreign exchange losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to overseas shareholders is deductible only if the debt-to-equity ratio does not exceed the thin capitalization limit (generally 2:1); a higher ratio requires demonstrating an arm's length interest rate and proper registration with SAFE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Profit - calculated as revenue minus costs and expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company reports continuous operating losses while the online store is highly profitable, the tax bureau may challenge the arm's length nature of management and royalty fees paid to the Taiwanese parent. Ensure the 'economic substance' of related-party transactions is documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjustment Increases - items such as non-deductible expenses, excess interest, and related-party adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must add back any withholding tax borne on behalf of the non-resident shareholder (e.g., if P&L contract states WHT on royalties is paid by WFOE) and any unapproved foreign-invoice amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt Income, Reduced Income, and Additional Deductions - includes interest from government bonds, qualified R&D super-deduction, and other incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D super-deduction for software development of the e-commerce platform must comply with the definition of R&D under the Ministry of Finance; no treaty benefit is available for Taiwan residents on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income - the base for computing tax; equals total profit after adjustments and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a permanent establishment (PE) is deemed to exist in Taiwan for the WFOE? Actually, China-source income taxed to the foreign parent is not included here; dividends repatriated to Taiwan are subject to WHT at the distribution stage, not to income tax in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Concessions - reduction of tax for preferential rates (e.g., small-scale or high-tech enterprise).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE has applied for HNTE status, the 15% rate applies; all incentive claims must be supported by certificates. Non-resident shareholders cannot directly claim Chinese domestic incentives on repatriated profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual Tax Payable / Refund - net tax after prepayments, credits, and foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any dispute between prepaid quarterly tax and final annual tax should be settled before the annual due date; late payments incur daily surcharge of 0.05% for both principal and prior surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: Article 62 of the Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) imposes fines ranging from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 (or higher when serious); late payment incurs a daily surcharge of 0.05% on the unpaid amount. Understating tax by more than 10% and above RMB 50%? Actually, criminal thresholds: evasion in excess of RMB 50,000 and more than 10% of the tax due can trigger criminal liability under Article 201 of the Criminal Law; penalties include fines and up to seven years imprisonment for significant evasion. Additionally, the PRC has a 'Tax Blacklist' system under which enterprise and responsible persons may face travel restrictions, revoked licenses, and public disclosure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (on gross dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder, unless reduced by a tax treaty that China has signed. Taiwan is not a party to any effective DTA with mainland China, so the 10% statutory rate applies.)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For jurisdictions with a bilateral treaty (not generally applicable to Taiwan), the non-resident shareholder must submit a 'Non-resident Taxpayer Application for Treatment under the Tax Agreement' (Form), together with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence tax authority, proof of beneficial ownership (e.g., not a conduit entity), and a statement of no permanent establishment in China. The payer (WFOE) must withhold at the reduced rate if the application is approved; alternatively, the full 10% is withheld and the taxpayer can apply for a refund through the local state tax bureau within three years. For Taiwan, since no DTA is in force, dividends distributed from the WFOE to the Taiwanese shareholder are subject to the full 10% WHT, and the Taiwanese shareholder may still claim an indirect foreign tax credit in its Taiwan corporate income tax filing to the extent allowed under Taiwanese law.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 10% for interest paid to non-residents; treaty rates may be 0%-10% if the recipient is a treaty-company resident. Royalties: statutory 10% for royalties derived from intellectual property licensed to a Chinese payer; treaty rates (e.g., 3%-10%) vary. Since Taiwan has no DTA with mainland China, interest and royalties remitted to a Taiwanese parent will be subject to the statutory 10% withholding. The withholding tax must be paid to the Chinese tax authority within 7 days of the remittance; failure to withhold triggers interest and penalties against the WFOE as the withholding agent.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation required if any single related-party transaction amount crosses: RMB 20 million for tangible asset transfers; RMB 10 million for intangible asset transfers (royalties); RMB 10 million for financial asset transfers; or RMB 40 million aggregate for other related-party transactions (e.g., services). Master File required if aggregate related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. The thresholds are defined in SAT Bulletin No. 42 (2016).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime similar to Cayman/BVI; however, under the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) of Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the recharacterization principle, the tax authority may disregard transactions or entities lacking economic substance. The company must demonstrate that it has real operations, employees, office space, and core income-generating activities (CIGA) in China for e-commerce, logistics, and customer support; payments to offshore affiliates for routine services should be supported by evidence of actual services performed. For a Taiwanese ultimate parent, the China WFOE must maintain a full set of operational records to avoid a challenge that it is a shell entity artificially transferring profits out of China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflating deductible expenses by using false or inflated vouchers such as purchased fake invoices (虚开发票) from shell suppliers, or omitting e-commerce sales income that was settled through personal PayPal or Stripe accounts not disclosed to the tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL), any person who fabricates, alters, conceals, or destroys accounting books or uses false invoices to underpay tax shall be ordered to pay the amount arbitrarily underpaid plus 50%-5 times the unpaid tax as a fine. Under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, tax evasion exceeding RMB 50,000 and more than 10% of the payable amount constitutes a criminal offense, punishable with imprisonment up to seven years plus fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where directors knowingly directed or deliberately allowed the false invoicing and underreporting. Directors can be held personally joint and several for the unpaid tax and penalties. In criminal cases, a responsible director faces imprisonment for up to 7 years, criminal fines, confiscation of personal assets, and a ban on serving as a director in any PRC-registered company for a designated period. The tax authority may also place the director on the 'Illegal Taxpayer Blacklist' (Tax Blacklist) triggering travel bans and denial of exit from China for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring intercompany royalty payments to an offshore entity (especially a Taiwanese affiliate) that has no employees, technical capacity, or economic substance to justify the package; or failing to prepare and maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation after crossing the statutory thresholds, causing profit shifting from China to a lower-tax/higher-benefit jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Entry Authority under Article 41 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law has the power to adjust taxable profits. Under Article 122 of the Implementation Rules, an adjustment will be subject to interest computed at the benchmark lending rate plus 5 percentage points per annum until the additional tax is paid. In severe cases, the inability to substantiate the transaction may be treated as fraudulent tax evasion, triggering fines up to 5 times the tax shortfall and criminal exposure under the Criminal Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the related-party agreements or knowingly sign false documentation can be held civilly liable for the tax and interest paid by the company. If the transfer pricing scheme is found to be a sham to evade tax, the director may face criminal charges for attempted tax evasion (imprisonment up to 7 years), personal fines, and disqualification as a director. Additionally, the tax authority can apply to have the director’s assets attached to satisfy unpaid tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Foreign Exchange Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using multiple bank accounts and structuring online payments from customers into offshore bank accounts to conceal the true revenue of the WFOE, or receiving international e-commerce settlement amounts in foreign currency and failing to repatriate them to the PRC within the statutory period without a valid SAFE filing; also intentionally omitting the source of large deposits to avoid AML scrutiny.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 191 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, money laundering is punishable by imprisonment of up to 10 years, with fines of up to 20% of the laundered amount and confiscation of criminal proceeds. Under the Anti-Money Laundering Law of the PRC, administrative fines of up to RMB 5 million can be imposed on the institution, and the responsible senior management may be fined up to RMB 500,000 individually. Violations of the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations may also lead to confiscation of illegal gains and fines up to 30% of the amount involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who facilitate, authorize, or fail to prevent the laundering scheme face personal criminal responsibility. Under Article 191, a director can be sentenced to imprisonment for up to 10 years, forfeiture of personal assets, and an order to pay restitution to the state for the tax evaded. The court may issue a travel ban and a no-exit order preventing the director from leaving China pending investigation. In addition, the director is disqualified from holding positions in financial institutions or being a legal representative of any Chinese company, and personal assets—including real estate and bank accounts—may be frozen and seized.
